/workspace/replays/5.py and /workspace/replays/5.log: SymPy 1.14.0 exact 3×3 generalized Gram derivation in edge-difference coordinates, six transfer polynomials and arithmetic example
correctness.rationale: Reversal transposes the product and the two outer factors commute, leaving two singular-spectrum classes. In the orthonormal disagreement basis whose first two vectors are the unit outer-edge differences, the outer updates are diagonal, with only their own entries changed from 1 to α=1−2p and γ=1−2r. The central update Q is I−qvv^T, with |v_1v_2|=1/2. In the difference between the two squared Frobenius norms all terms except the interaction of those two coordinates cancel, giving Q_12²(1−α²)(1−γ²)=δ. The second Gram coefficient is the squared Frobenius norm of the three-dimensional adjugate, and the same comparison gives δ: the outer adjugate diagonals are (1,α,α) and (γ,1,γ), while adj(Q)_12=−Q_12. Adjugate identities hold also when a rate is 1/2. Gram determinants agree by multiplicativity, giving δλ(1−λ). All eigenvalues of each disagreement Gram are below 1 since norm preservation would require all three edge equalities on a mean-zero input. The batched factor β is positive since (in the batched order) some endpoint entry is zero whereas J has all entries positive. The serial polynomial is positive throughout [β,1), excluding a Gram root there, and proving W_S<W_B. The arithmetic case and common transfer polynomial agree; cyclic determinant invariance requires no nonsingularity. The proof and exact replay handle general strengths, not just the numerical grid.
residual_risks: No conclusion at the excluded endpoints or for longer/repeated sweeps follows from this comparison.
